result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.dispersion()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate dispersion between two nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L8515-L8612){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.dispersion( u, v, normalized=True, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Dispersion measures the embeddedness of a link in the network. A link between two nodes (`u` and `v`) has high dispersion when their mutual neighbors (friends in common) are not well connected to each other. This can indicate structural diversity in the network. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [u]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Source node (node ID or label). [v]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Target node (node ID or label). [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), normalize by the number of common neighbors (embeddedness). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The dispersion score between `u` and `v`. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Dispersion, introduced by Backstrom and Kleinberg (2014), asks a subtler question than raw neighbor overlap: given the common neighbors of two nodes, how *dispersed* are they across the rest of the network? If the shared neighbors are themselves tightly interlinked, the tie between $u$ and $v$ sits in a dense cluster and dispersion is low; if those neighbors are far from one another in the residual graph, the tie spans different regions and dispersion is high. That property made it strikingly effective in its original application, spotting romantic partners in social-network data, where such ties bridge otherwise distinct friendship circles even when embeddedness is high. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Dispersion tends to be higher when a link's shared connections aren't well connected to each other -- a sign the two nodes bridge otherwise separate parts of the network: ::: {#fcb1b5b1 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() for i in range(1, 6): graph.add_node() for s, t in [(1, 2), (1, 3), (1, 4), (2, 3), (2, 5), (3, 4), (3, 5), (4, 5)]: graph.add_edge(s, t) disp = graph.dispersion(1, 2) f"Dispersion: {disp:.2f}" ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 'Dispersion: 0.00' ``` ::: ::: Labels work just as well as raw node IDs: ::: {#420ddbf2 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_node(label="Alice") graph.add_node(label="Bob") graph.add_node(label="Charlie") graph.add_node(label="David") alice = graph.get_id_from_label("Alice") bob = graph.get_id_from_label("Bob") charlie = graph.get_id_from_label("Charlie") david = graph.get_id_from_label("David") graph.add_edge(alice, bob) graph.add_edge(alice, charlie) graph.add_edge(bob, charlie) graph.add_edge(bob, david) disp = graph.dispersion(alice, bob, normalized=True) f"Dispersion: {disp:.2f}" ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 'Dispersion: 0.00' ``` ::: ::: `normalized=False` returns the raw embeddedness count rather than dividing it by the number of common neighbors: ::: {#4452a2c7 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_cycle_graph(6) nodes = sorted(graph.get_node_ids()) norm = graph.dispersion(nodes[0], nodes[1], normalized=True) unnorm = graph.dispersion(nodes[0], nodes[1], normalized=False) f"Normalized: {norm:.2f}, Unnormalized: {unnorm}" ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 'Normalized: 0.00, Unnormalized: 0.0' ``` ::: :::
